text:
maya: Heads-up: working on a grafana dashboard to combine per-tenant billing tags with GPU metrics to cut alert noise. Trying to map k8s tenant labels -> node exporter metrics. Anyone seen prior work?

aj: we had a proto last quarter. main issue was label cardinality when joining tenant labels to per-gpu metrics. we used recording rules to roll up per-tenant totals which helped a lot.

derek: Can you paste the promql you plan to use? also what's the expected traffic shape — short bursts or steady?

maya: Mostly short bursts, many tenants spike for <2m. plan is to avoid per-gpu series explosion by recording a per-tenant series. basic idea: create a recording rule that sums allocations by tenant and stores as `gpu_allocated_seconds_by_tenant`. example recording rule snippet:```yaml
- record: gpu_allocated_seconds_by_tenant
  expr: sum by (tenant) (gpu_seconds_total)
```

lexi: For bursts use `increase(...)` or `rate(...)` with a short window and a non-zero `for:` in the alert to prevent flapping. Also consider `max_over_time`/`quantile_over_time` for stability on dashboards.

maya: thanks — thinking alerts should be burn-rate style per-tenant SLOs: if tenant consumes > X% of commit in a short window then page. want to avoid paging on 30s blips so `for: 10m` or `for: 15m` seems right.

aj: we also added canonical billing tags in the billing pipeline; make sure panels and alerts use `billing_tenant` label so names match across systems. also add a fallback for untagged series.

omar: ops notes: 1) reduce prometheus series by doing `sum(...) by (tenant)` in recording rules not at query time. 2) in Grafana use transforms to coalesce `tenant` names from multiple sources. 3) limit label sets to {tenant, region, host_type} to keep cardinality low.

maya: proposed alert expression (draft):
```promql
sum by (tenant) (increase(gpu_seconds_total[5m])) > (tenant_commit_gpu_seconds * 0.25)
```
with `for: 10m` and a soft severity (p3) to start. fallback for missing `tenant_commit_gpu_seconds` using a scalar default is needed.

derek: looks good. watch out for tenants without `tenant_commit_gpu_seconds` label. fallback pattern: `tenant_commit_gpu_seconds or scalar(3600)` or use `coalesce` logic in the recording rule.

lexi: :thumbsup: I'll mock a dashboard with these panels: 1) per-tenant burn (line + threshold), 2) top-10 bursters (bar), 3) eviction-risk vs temperature scatter, 4) billing-tag coverage heatmap across regions. I'll export the panel JSON once it's stable.

maya: also want a panel that correlates `gpu_eviction_risk` with billing spikes so we can tell if high-cost tenants are causing evictions. a small opacity histogram helps visual spotting.

sre-bot: Ticket created: INF-4321 - tenant billing rollup dashboard + alert tuning. link: https://tickets.redwood/INF-4321 :white_check_mark:

omar: one more ops suggestion: mute alerts for low-commit tenants (commits < X) and only page on high-eviction-risk (`gpu_eviction_risk > 0.6`) or sustained over-usage. also route high-sev to oncall only if eviction risk present.

maya: great, will iterate. I'll post the dashboard JSON & alert rules by EOD and drop a link here. thanks all.

(Notes: include `recording rules` in prometheus to avoid expensive cross-label joins at query time; prefer storing the rollups and using those in Grafana. keep panel queries simple: read recorded `gpu_allocated_seconds_by_tenant` and join on `billing_tenant` label.)
